title: A colimit cocone is initial relative to restriction of its base
statement:
Use coherent diagrams, transformations, mapping spaces and colimiting cocones of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Let $K$ be a small simplicial set and $\mathcal E$ a quasicategory in a containing universe. Define the right join cone $K^{\triangleright}=K\star\Delta^0$: its simplices are those of either factor and the ordered concatenations of a simplex of $K$ with a simplex at the new final vertex. Write
$$r:\operatorname{Fun}(K^{\triangleright},\mathcal E)\to\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal E)$$
for restriction. Let $c:K^{\triangleright}\to\mathcal E$ be a simplicial map. Its induced coherent cocone is obtained by precomposition with $K\times\Delta^1\to K^{\triangleright}$, splitting each interval simplex at its change from $0$ to $1$, retaining its initial $K$-vertices and sending its final vertices to the cone vertex. If that coherent cocone is colimiting, then for every simplicial map $t:K^{\triangleright}\to\mathcal E$, restriction induces a weak homotopy equivalence of Kan complexes
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(K^{\triangleright},\mathcal E)}(c,t)\ \longrightarrow\ \operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal E)}(c|_K,t|_K).$$
The base diagram of $t$ is arbitrary, and need not equal $c|_K$.

source.place: Proposition 7.1.6.13, colimit dual with target base a point: the cone is initial relative to restriction. The join-to-coherent-cocone convention is the opposite dual of the fixed-boundary comparison in lem-coef-infinity-join-cone-calculus (Kerodon 4.6.6.8). Read online; not archived. Kerodon tag, not a Stacks tag.

proof.text:
Put $D=\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal E)$. Define the opposite of a simplicial set $S$ by $S^{\mathrm{op}}_n=S_n$, with the operator for $\alpha:[m]\to[n]$ given by the original operator for $\alpha^{\mathrm{rev}}(i)=n-\alpha(m-i)$. Reversal takes $\Lambda_i^n$ to $\Lambda_{n-i}^n$, hence preserves quasicategories. It exchanges the two blocks in a join and exchanges the interval endpoints, giving
$$(K\star\Delta^0)^{\mathrm{op}}=\Delta^0\star K^{\mathrm{op}},\qquad \operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal E)^{\mathrm{op}}\cong\operatorname{Fun}(K^{\mathrm{op}},\mathcal E^{\mathrm{op}}).$$
For the second identification reverse the parameter simplex as well as $K$. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-join-cone-calculus] to $K^{\mathrm{op}},\mathcal E^{\mathrm{op}}$ and take opposites. The joint apex-and-boundary comparison becomes an equivalence from $\operatorname{Fun}(K^{\triangleright},\mathcal E)$ to
$$\mathcal T^+_K=D\times_{D,\operatorname{ev}_0}\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,D)\times_{\operatorname{ev}_1,D}\mathcal E,$$
where the first $D\to D$ is the identity and $\mathcal E\to D$ is $\Delta_K$. Its objects are $(x,F,\lambda:F\to\Delta_Kx)$. Reversal of the fat-cone map retains the initial $K$-vertices labelled $0$ and sends the final vertices labelled $1$ to the apex. It is therefore exactly the comparison prescribed in the item, with both the apex and the boundary retained.

Mapping spaces under this reversal must be compared as homotopy types, not identified as right-pinched simplicial sets. Use [lem-coef-infinity-pinch-comparison]: its natural equivalences identify right-pinched $\operatorname{Map}$ with the arrow spaces $U$. Reversing the arrow interval gives $U_{\mathcal A^{\mathrm{op}}}(v,u)\cong U_{\mathcal A}(u,v)^{\mathrm{op}}$. For every simplicial set $S$, reversing barycentric coordinates gives a natural homeomorphism $|S^{\mathrm{op}}|\cong|S|$; its compatibility with realization relations is the formula for $\alpha^{\mathrm{rev}}$ above. These comparisons preserve the projections induced by apex and boundary restriction. Reversing the path interval in the homotopy-pullback formula gives the dual formula
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal T^+_K}((x,F,\lambda),(y,G,\mu))\simeq\operatorname{Map}_D(F,G)\mathop{\times}^{h}_{\operatorname{Map}_D(F,\Delta_Ky)}\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal E}(x,y),$$
with maps $b\mapsto\mu b$ and $a\mapsto\Delta_K(a)\lambda$: both composites go from $F$ to $\Delta_Ky$. Reversal retains the path and all its parameter simplices. By [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] the comparison equivalence induces mapping-space equivalences. Thus the displayed formula also computes the join-diagram mapping space, and its projection to $\operatorname{Map}_D(F,G)$ is the actual restriction map. No boundary diagram has been fixed in this formula.

proof.text:
Let $c$ correspond to $(x,F,\lambda)$. Its induced coherent cocone $\lambda:F	o\Delta_Kx$ is colimiting by hypothesis. Apply the cocone dual of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus]. For every $y\in\mathcal E$ and cocone $
u:F	o\Delta_Ky$, that statement identifies the mapping space from $\lambda$ to $
u$ in the fixed-$F$ cocone category with the homotopy fiber over $
u$ of
$$q_y:\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal E}(x,y)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Map}_D(F,\Delta_Ky),\qquad a\longmapsto\Delta_K(a)\lambda.$$
Initiality in that cocone category, as defined in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], says these mapping spaces are contractible. The same cited calculus states the equivalent colimit criterion: $q_y$ is an equivalence for every $y$. This uses the fixed-boundary cocone mapping formula from that node, rather than taking the fiber of Step 1's varying-boundary formula without justification. It includes an empty target mapping space: if the latter is empty, a point of the source would map to a point of it, so both are empty.

source.place: Agent-written application of the cocone dual of lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus; the fixed-fiber stage corresponds to Kerodon 02XB, first paragraph of proof.

proof.text: For arbitrary $t$ let its triple be $(y,G,\mu)$ and set $B=\operatorname{Map}_D(F,G)$, $Z=\operatorname{Map}_D(F,\Delta_Ky)$, and $A=\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal E}(x,y)$. Step 1 identifies the source mapping space, with restriction to $B$, with $B\times_Z^h A$ for the maps $b\mapsto\mu b$ and $q_y:A\to Z$. Step 2 says $q_y$ is a weak equivalence. Here is the precise base-change argument using [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper]. Factor $q_y$ as a weak equivalence $A\to\widetilde A$ followed by a Kan fibration $p:\widetilde A\to Z$. Two-out-of-three makes $p$ a weak equivalence too. The homotopy pullback is represented by $B\times_Z\widetilde A$, and its projection to $B$ is the pullback of the trivial fibration $p$. A lifting square for this projection against a boundary inclusion is the corresponding square for $p$ with the $B$-coordinate already prescribed, so it has a filler. The projection is consequently a trivial fibration and a weak equivalence by the cited model-structure statement. Under the natural boundary-projected equivalence of [lem-coef-infinity-join-cone-calculus] from Step 1, this proves that the actual restriction map to $B=\operatorname{Map}_D(c|_K,t|_K)$ is a weak equivalence. There is no assumption $G=F$.

source.place: Agent-written homotopy-pullback argument from the stated Kan model structure; proves the relative-initiality conclusion of Kerodon 02XB by a different route from its cocartesian-fibration proof.

proof.text: By [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus], both $\operatorname{Fun}(K^{\triangleright},\mathcal E)$ and $D=\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal E)$ are quasicategories and their right-pinched mapping spaces are Kan complexes. In degree $n$, the map between those mapping spaces is precomposition with $K\hookrightarrow K^{\triangleright}$ on the $K$-factor of each functor simplex. This is precisely the boundary projection retained in Step 1, so Step 3 proves the asserted weak homotopy equivalence of Kan complexes for every $t$.
